summary: House records document three official Wayne Owens Middle East trips in 1988.
detail: Quarterly House Foreign Affairs travel tables record Owens in Egypt on February 14, across Greece, Egypt, Bahrain, Jordan, and Israel on April 3-13, and across Egypt, Saudi Arabia, Iraq, Jordan, Syria, and Israel on December 7-22. Owens's March 9, 1989 floor statement independently described the December trip and two earlier official visits in 1988. The tables identify Owens but do not provide delegation lists.
source_quote: my December trip and my two earlier official visits last year

summary: Contemporaneous reporting documents a separate Owens trip to Tunis in February 1989.
detail: The Deseret News reached Owens during his return through New York on February 14, 1989 and reported that he had met Yasser Arafat and other PLO officials in Tunisia for more than four hours the previous day. No traveling companion or payer was identified, and no Owens entry was located in the reviewed 1989 quarterly House Foreign Affairs travel tables.
source_quote: upon his return from Tunisia, where he met with Arafat

target_name: Wayne Owens / Middle East Development Bank trip
summary: Contemporaneous reports date Owens's four-country development-bank trip to approximately March 23-April 5, 1989, without naming Epstein.
detail: Departure and return reporting documents a roughly ten-day Owens trip through Egypt, Jordan, Saudi Arabia, and Israel to promote a Middle East development bank. The reports name meetings with Hosni Mubarak, Chaim Herzog, King Hussein, King Fahd, Shimon Peres, ministers, and businesspeople. They do not name Jeffrey Epstein or any traveling companion. This establishes the trip but not that it is the trip recalled by participants in 2025.
source_quote: he departed for an 11-day trip to Egypt, Jordan, Saudi Arabia and Israel

target_name: Wayne Owens / Middle East travel census
summary: A later aggregate count implies two additional, still-undated Owens Middle East trips in 1989-1990.
detail: A 1991 Deseret News summary of a Roll Call Report Syndicate study says Owens took seven taxpayer-funded foreign trips in 1989-1990: six to the Middle East and one eight-day Soviet trip. Four Middle East trips in that period are individually dated in the present reconstruction, leaving two count-derived slots. Because the underlying Roll Call table was not located and the quarterly House travel tables are not exhaustive, the dates and itineraries remain unresolved.
source_quote: All of those trips were to the Middle East, except one eight-day trip to the Soviet Union.

target_name: Wayne Owens / Middle East Development Bank
summary: Owens introduced H.J.Res. 213 on March 21, 1989; it received referrals but no recorded hearing or markup.
detail: H.J.Res. 213 proposed a Middle East Development Bank to foster regional development and economic cooperation. Congress.gov records zero cosponsors and referral on April 3 to two House Foreign Affairs subcommittees, with executive comment requested from State and Treasury. No hearing, witness list, markup, committee report, or later action is recorded.
source_quote: To establish a Middle East Development Bank.

summary: Owens's March 9, 1989 floor statement named the development-bank idea sources and did not name Epstein.
detail: Owens said he had helped S. Daniel Abraham organize the Center for Middle East Peace and Economic Cooperation the previous month. He credited development-bank ideas to Abraham, David Jan Mitchell, Joyce Starr, Representatives Lee Hamilton, Henry Waxman, and Mel Levine, among others. Jeffrey Epstein is not named. The omission is bounded to this public explanation and is not a participant-list null.
source_quote: Many of the ideas for this project come from S. Daniel Abraham

summary: A March 1989 floor submission contemporaneously documents Gordon's Israel experience and policy relationship with Owens.
detail: Owens entered Dan Gordon's tripartite-confederacy proposal into the Congressional Record on March 8, 1989. Owens described Gordon as a friend, a Jewish American who had lived in Israel as a kibbutznik for nine years, served in the Israeli Defense Forces, and was a screenwriter and Southern California community leader. This explains a policy role but does not document Gordon on a trip.
source_quote: Dan Gordon, a good friend of mine, is a Jewish American who lived in Israel

summary: FEC records show two distinct $1,000 Jeffrey Epstein contributions to Wayne Owens's committee on June 22, 1990.
detail: The FEC Schedule A API returns exactly two non-amended receipts from EPSTEIN, JEFFREY, New York NY 10022, employer field INVESTMENT BANKER, to the Wayne Owens for Congress Committee (C00199992). Each receipt was $1,000 on June 22, 1990. Their sub-IDs are 3061920110002393468 and 3061920110002393469. This is a primary financial edge but does not establish travel funding or quid pro quo.

summary: University of Utah catalogs identify Owens's papers and concrete photograph folders for 1989 Tunis and 1990 Middle East travel.
detail: The Wayne Owens papers are MS 0108 at the J. Willard Marriott Library. The separate P0108 photograph finding aid identifies International Travel in boxes 12-16, Tunis 1989 in box 12 folder 11, Egypt and Greece/Macedonia circa 1989-1993 in box 12 folder 3, and a 1990 Middle East trip album in box 2 folder 11. These are catalog references; the materials were not inspected.

target_name: Jeffrey Epstein / Wayne Owens trip provenance
summary: No public telling of the Epstein-Owens trip by Gordon or Yeager was located before the December 16, 2025 New York Times investigation.
detail: Exact-name and distinctive-phrase searches of the open web, Deseret News archive, and public JTA archive found no Dan Gordon or Michael Yeager public account of Epstein traveling with Owens before December 16, 2025. Later republications and podcasts trace to the same New York Times investigation. This is a bounded public-index null, not proof that no earlier private or unindexed account exists.
